author: Vox
description:
Social media was once hailed as a powerful weapon against authoritarianism. Then came misinformation, online censorship, and a growing consensus that it was doing more harm to democracy than good.

But new protest movements in India and Hungary are complicating that story. Vox’s Zack Beauchamp explains why social media may still be a force for democracy — especially in countries experiencing democratic backsliding.

author: Vox
description:
When talking to voters about older elected officials, one concern comes up again and again: In an age of AI and rapid technological change, can longtime lawmakers keep up?

On America, Actually, Vox’s Astead Herndon asks 86-year-old Rep. Jim Clyburn (D-SC) how he can effectively legislate on technology he has never used — and, until recently, had barely heard of.

author: Vox
description:
For years, right-wing influencers and politicians have pushed the conservative movement to have more controversial, anti-establishment views. Why are some of those figures now upset about where the movement has ended up?

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In today’s episode, guest host Bryan Walsh speaks with Vox Senior Correspondent Zack Beauchamp about conservatives who decry the extremist direction that the right is moving but refuse to recognize the role they played in pushing the movement in that direction. The two discuss US Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY), pundit Ben Shapiro, podcaster Candace Owens, the drivers of conservative extremism, and what the party might look like after Donald Trump.
